media_strategy.selection_principle: Rich-media run defaulting to all five channels. Primary imagery is 18 VERIFIED real Wikimedia company logos used in a filterable company-card deck and a funding leaderboard; 12 confirmed mismatch logos were dropped and those companies (plus 20 not-found) render as clean CSS typographic wordmark cards. AI media (one abstract hero + one motion clip) provides atmosphere for the power-law funding story; a generated ambient bed closes the piece. Each channel is chosen to fit the dataset, not a quota.

chart.reason: Funding leaderboard (power law), geography distribution, founding-year timeline and category count-vs-capital inversion are all decisive quantitative comparisons drawn from analyst data_tables.

image.reason: Primary imagery is 18 REAL Wikimedia logos (credited per-card and in Sources) in a filterable deck + leaderboard. One AI abstract hero ('two pillars of light over a field of nodes') literally visualizes the 79.4% funding concentration.

video.reason: A 5s text2video clip animates the gold-rush / power-law motif as the full-bleed teaser — motion conveys the towering-pillars concentration a still cannot. (image2video on the hero was attempted first but the veo service was under high load; fell back to text2video seedance-2.0 — see media_blockers.)

audio.reason: A generated ambient tech soundscape plays as a reader-controlled bed in the closing section, evoking a quiet capital frontier. Non-autoplay with a visual caption fallback.

interactive_or_map.reason: A guess-first quiz on the OpenAI+Anthropic funding share (the surprising 79.4%) and a filterable real-logo company card deck (filter by category). Geography shown as a chart rather than a fake map — the data is city names, well served by a ranked bar.

media_blockers.reason: image2video (google/veo-3.1-fast) returned 'service experiencing high load' twice on the hero still.
media_blockers.fallback_des: des_12 — used text2video (bytedance/seedance-2.0) to generate teaser.mp4 from a matching prompt instead; succeeded.

des_01.label: Teaser — power-law gold-rush motion clip

content.prompt: Abstract cinematic visualization of an AI gold rush: a dark navy field filled with hundreds of tiny faint twinkling teal nodes, and two enormous radiant pillars of golden-white light slowly rising and pulsing far above the rest, dwarfing everything. Slow push-in, drifting particle bokeh, volumetric fog, luminous gold and teal palette, editorial tech mood, no text, no logos.

des_01.brief: Full-viewport teaser. Looping muted clip of two towering pillars of light over a field of faint nodes — a visual metaphor for two companies holding 79.4% of the money. Headline overlaid at the bottom with a dark scrim. Poster fallback is hero.png.
des_01.rationale: Motion sells the dwarfing effect; the two pillars are the whole thesis in one image before a word is read.

des_02.label: Hero still (poster + atmospheric image)

content.prompt: A striking abstract visualization of an AI gold rush and extreme capital concentration: a vast dark field of hundreds of tiny faint glowing nodes, and two enormous radiant pillars of golden-white light towering above them. Deep navy-to-black gradient, volumetric fog, fine particle bokeh, luminous teal and warm gold palette, editorial tech aesthetic, no text, no logos.

des_02.brief: Serves as the teaser video poster/fallback. Two golden light pillars dwarf a field of dim nodes — the power-law concentration made visible.
des_02.rationale: A strong still is needed as the video poster and as the no-JS / mobile fallback for the teaser.

des_03.label: Guess-first quiz — what share do the top 2 hold?

content.initial_state: Prompt: 'Of all $305.7B raised by the 50 companies, what share do the top two (OpenAI + Anthropic) hold?' with four choices: ~25%, ~50%, ~65%, ~79%.
content.transition: Choices lock; the correct option (79%) highlights gold; a short reveal panel fades in.
content.payoff: Reveal: 79.4% — two companies out of fifty. The mean ($6.1B) is 8.3x the median ($735M).

des_03.brief: Four-button guess-first quiz. Most readers guess far too low, which makes the 79.4% reveal land. Reveal panel cites the exact figures from ana_02/ana_03.
des_03.rationale: The concentration is surprising — letting the reader commit to a guess maximizes the shock of the real number, better than opening with a static chart.

des_04.label: OpenAI+Anthropic share stat callout

content.label: of all $305.7B raised is held by just two companies — OpenAI and Anthropic

des_04.brief: Large 64px gold stat under the quiz, restating the headline figure.
des_04.rationale: The number is striking enough to stand alone as a headline stat.

des_05.label: Funding leaderboard — full power-law bar chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip with exact $ value; log-friendly note that OpenAI/Anthropic bars are clipped in scale

des_05.brief: Full 50-company horizontal bar chart sorted descending by funding (millions USD). OpenAI and Anthropic bars are highlighted gold and visibly dwarf the rest; the long flat tail is the point. Tooltip shows exact $M. Use a sqrt or log-ish visual treatment OR keep linear but let the two giants run off — the dwarfing IS the message; label OpenAI 182,600 and Anthropic 60,000 explicitly.
des_05.rationale: The single most important finding (the power law) deserves the full leaderboard; showing all 50 makes the tail undeniable.

des_06.label: Two-giants-vs-tail stat callout

content.label: of the list has raised under $1 billion; only 18 of 50 have crossed it

des_06.brief: Secondary stat callout reinforcing the long tail.
des_06.rationale: Pairs the headline concentration with the tail's scale.

des_07.label: Geography distribution chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip with count and pct

des_07.brief: Four-bar horizontal chart: San Francisco (25, 50%), Rest of Bay Area / CA (8), Rest of US (11), International (6). San Francisco bar highlighted. Shows one city = half the list.
des_07.rationale: The data is city/region names, best read as a ranked bar; a literal map would scatter dots without adding insight, so a clean bar wins.

des_08.label: Founding-year timeline histogram

content.interaction: hover tooltip with count; annotation marking late-2022 ChatGPT inflection

des_08.brief: Vertical column chart of company count by founding year 2013-2025, with 2022 (the peak, 11 companies) highlighted and a small annotation at the late-2022 ChatGPT moment. The post-2020 surge should be visually obvious.
des_08.rationale: Founding years are a time series — a column timeline reads instantly and lets the 2022 spike speak.

des_09.label: Category count chart
des_09.brief: Horizontal bar of company COUNT by application category (Generative media 8, Foundation models 7, Infrastructure 7, Agents 6, Coding 5, ...). Establishes the breadth of applied AI by headcount.
des_09.rationale: Sets up the inversion in des_10 — readers see breadth here, then narrowness in capital next.

des_10.label: Category capital chart — the inversion

content.interaction: hover tooltip with exact $M and % of total

des_10.brief: Horizontal bar of total FUNDING by category. Foundation models ($254.4B) dwarfs everything; highlighted gold. Placed directly after the count chart so the reader sees the same categories reorder violently — breadth by count, narrowness by capital.
des_10.rationale: The juxtaposition of count vs capital is the turn of the whole piece; two paired charts make the inversion visceral.

des_11.label: Company card deck — verified logos + wordmarks, filterable

content.initial_state: A responsive grid of 50 company cards. 18 cards show a REAL verified logo on a light tile; the other 32 show a clean CSS typographic wordmark (company name set in a strong display style on a tinted tile). Each card shows name, category tag, funding, and founding year.
content.trigger: Reader clicks a category filter chip (All, Foundation models, Generative media, Infrastructure, Agents, Coding, Robotics, Healthcare, Legal & finance, Other).
content.transition: Cards not matching the filter fade/collapse out with a short transition; matching cards reflow.
content.payoff: The reader can browse the whole list as faces, see which categories are crowded, and read each company's funding/year at a glance.

des_11.brief: VISUAL CENTERPIECE. 50-card filterable deck. Verified-logo cards (18): Anthropic, Applied Intuition, Cohere, Cursor, Databricks, ElevenLabs, Glean, HeyGen, Lovable, Mistral AI, Notion, OpenAI, OpenEvidence, Perplexity, Physical Intelligence, Replit, Runway, Suno — each logo on a white/light rounded tile with a small 'logo: Wikimedia' credit, max-height constrained, object-fit contain. Wordmark cards (32): company name in a bold condensed display treatment on a navy/teal-tinted tile (NOT a fake logo). Every card carries category tag + funding ($) + year. Filter chips along the top filter by category. The card data (name, category, funding, year, has_logo, logo_file) should be inlined as a JS array built from ana_02 (funding), ana_06 (years), ana_07 (categories) and ana_11 (logo coverage).
des_11.rationale: A 50-item list of comparable entities is exactly what a filterable card deck is for; real logos as primary imagery, honest wordmarks for the rest. This is the page's richest, most browsable moment.

des_12.label: Verified-logo credit note
des_12.brief: Not a standalone image — this item carries the per-logo attribution table for the 18 verified logos used in the card deck (des_11). The Programmer renders these credits in a compact Sources block under the deck and in the References section. Every used logo is credited to Wikimedia Commons with artist + license.
des_12.rationale: Attribution requirement: every real logo used must be credited.

des_13.label: Closing ambient soundscape bed

content.why_audio: A quiet ambient bed turns the closing caveats into a contemplative outro — the sound of a frontier mid-break — rather than a dry disclaimer list.
content.trigger: Click a play button in the closing section (never autoplay).
content.ui_form: section-integrated mini-player: a slim play/pause control inside the closing chapter, with a one-line caption.

content.prompt: Ambient minimal tech soundscape, slow and contemplative, soft warm synth pads, distant glassy bell tones rising like a slow gold-rush dawn, gentle low drone, no drums, no vocals, cinematic and restrained, 30 seconds.

content.fallback: If audio is muted or unsupported, the closing prose stands alone; the play button shows a caption describing the bed.
content.novelty_note: Not a tone card and not a sonification gimmick — a restrained reader-controlled bed scoped to the final chapter only.

des_13.brief: Reader-controlled 30s ambient bed in the closing section. Slim mini-player, non-autoplay, with caption fallback.
des_13.rationale: Audio earns its slot as atmosphere for the close; a sonification would feel forced on a funding ranking already shown as a bar chart.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial, luminous gold-and-teal on near-black navy — a 'capital frontier at night' mood
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first teaser, then text → chart/interactive alternating; the card deck is the browsable centerpiece
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Centerpiece is a filterable real-logo card deck, not a chart; the teaser is a power-law metaphor video; audio is a scoped closing bed, not a tone card. Two paired charts (count vs capital) create a deliberate inversion rather than a chart streak.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Large gold stat callouts (56-64px); system-ui for UI/labels and wordmark cards (bold condensed); Georgia serif for body. Section kickers in letterspaced uppercase teal.
